pr.title: fix: memory leak in notebook text diff editor
pr.body: ### Details Notebook diff view models were registered in the editor pane's lifetime disposable store, so closing a notebook diff editor left every previous view model and its notebook models reachable. ### Change Register each notebook diff view model in the input-specific store and run the existing model-detach cleanup when the editor input is cleared. ### Before When opening and closing a notebook diff editor 37 times, notebook diff view models and their notebook models grow once or twice per run: ### After No more notebook diff view model or notebook model leak is detected. ### Test Video [test-video.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/12aac422-2354-4abe-9f39-1ed9efb36a71)

reviews.body: ## Pull request overview Fixes notebook diff editor model leaks by aligning disposables with each editor input’s lifetime. **Changes:** - Disposes layout work during model detachment. - Registers diff view models in the input-specific disposable store. - Reuses model-detachment cleanup when clearing input. --- 💡 Configure MCP servers for context-aware, tailored reviews. Learn more in the docs.
Verified the diff. Changes align with project standards.

### 🟡 Changes recommended Detaching does not cancel in-flight layout work, and the ownership fix lacks regression coverage.
2 open findings - [Cancel pending diff work when detaching the input](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/331805#discussion_r4264575073) · New - [Test disposal of view-model and dispatcher on input replacement](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/331805#discussion_r4264575152) · New
1 resolved since last review - [Dispose the model-scoped dispatcher before dropping this reference.…](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/331805#discussion_r3822652981)
🧠 **Review effort:** Balanced

comments.body:
### P3: reset the current-change index when clearing an input

The new [`clearInput()` → `_detachModel()` call](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b1f5219afb895af7a84c5412c8b127dbe7852205/src/vs/workbench/contrib/notebook/browser/diff/notebookDiffEditor.ts#L925) changes an observable-state side effect: [the input-local store is now cleared](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b1f5219afb895af7a84c5412c8b127dbe7852205/src/vs/workbench/contrib/notebook/browser/diff/notebookDiffEditor.ts#L532) before [the list is cleared](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b1f5219afb895af7a84c5412c8b127dbe7852205/src/vs/workbench/contrib/notebook/browser/diff/notebookDiffEditor.ts#L544). That removes [the focus subscription that resets `currentChangedIndex` to `-1`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b1f5219afb895af7a84c5412c8b127dbe7852205/src/vs/workbench/contrib/notebook/browser/diff/notebookDiffEditor.ts#L574) before it receives the empty-focus event.

Previously, clearing the input spliced the list while that subscription was still alive. With this change, a cached pane can retain the previous input's current-change index. This observable is consumed by [the chat notebook-diff integration](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b1f5219afb895af7a84c5412c8b127dbe7852205/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatEditing/notebook/chatEditingNotebookEditorIntegration.ts#L687), including [navigation-boundary decisions](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b1f5219afb895af7a84c5412c8b127dbe7852205/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatEditing/notebook/chatEditingNotebookEditorIntegration.ts#L715), so it is not just an unused field.

**Suggested repro / regression test (source-derived; not executed):**
1. Use the notebook text-diff editor (`notebook.experimental.enableNewDiffEditor: false`, `notebook.diff.enablePreview: true`).
2. Open a notebook diff with at least three changed cells and focus the third change; verify its current-change index is `2`.
3. Close that diff while retaining the editor group/pane cache. In a debugger or a scoped pane test, inspect the same pane immediately after input clearing completes, before another list update.
4. Expected: the index is `-1`. The new disposal ordering leaves it at `2`. Replacing the input in the same group also carries that stale state until an applicable items/focus update resets it.

Could the detach path explicitly reset the observable, with a focused clear/reuse test? That would preserve the new input-specific ownership without depending on a listener that has already been disposed.

**Validation limit:** the ordering and only-writer relationship were checked statically; I have not reproduced a visible chat-navigation failure. The pane's own next/previous navigation uses list focus and is not claimed broken.

### Race-coverage request: clearing the layout token before the final set-input continuation

This is a **lower-confidence validation concern, not a reproduced user-visible regression**.

The new [assignment clearing the layout cancellation source](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b1f5219afb895af7a84c5412c8b127dbe7852205/src/vs/workbench/contrib/notebook/browser/diff/notebookDiffEditor.ts#L531) needs to be considered alongside the [await of modified-webview creation](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b1f5219afb895af7a84c5412c8b127dbe7852205/src/vs/workbench/contrib/notebook/browser/diff/notebookDiffEditor.ts#L514) and the subsequent [unguarded `.token` dereference](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b1f5219afb895af7a84c5412c8b127dbe7852205/src/vs/workbench/contrib/notebook/browser/diff/notebookDiffEditor.ts#L519).

**Suggested deterministic interleaving for a scoped test (not executed):**
1. Begin setting a resolved notebook-diff input.
2. Hold the continuation at the modified-webview await using a test-controlled promise, after the helper has created the webview.
3. Clear/close that input, then release the continuation without attaching a replacement input.
4. Assert that the obsolete open operation completes without dereferencing a cleared source. With the new assignment, the resumed expression can throw a TypeError before reaching [the no-model guard inside `updateLayout()`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b1f5219afb895af7a84c5412c8b127dbe7852205/src/vs/workbench/contrib/notebook/browser/diff/notebookDiffEditor.ts#L648). Before this change, that source remained present and this particular continuation could reach the guard and return.

An input/model-staleness check after the await, before accessing the source, would make the intended close-during-open behavior explicit.

**Scope/limitations:** the real helper currently has no internal await, so normal UI reachability of this microtask interleaving is unverified; the proposed test deliberately controls it. There is already a similar earlier-await failure involving a cleared model, so this is not a claim that the PR introduced the broader cancellation problem. Please treat this as a narrowly scoped test/guard request, not a confirmed general cancellation regression.
Created a separate PR to handle cancellation of diffEditorInputs better: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339389

### P3: the change index still survives input clearing at the current head

Following up on [the earlier index-reset finding](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/331805#issuecomment-5882360111): this remains present at current head `44a225758b78438ccca2a32e94e1871cc845cdd9`, after the lifecycle changes were reverted.

The new [`clearInput()` -> `_detachModel()` call](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/44a225758b78438ccca2a32e94e1871cc845cdd9/src/vs/workbench/contrib/notebook/browser/diff/notebookDiffEditor.ts#L925) changes the reset ordering:

1. [`_localStore.clear()`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/44a225758b78438ccca2a32e94e1871cc845cdd9/src/vs/workbench/contrib/notebook/browser/diff/notebookDiffEditor.ts#L532) disposes [the focus listener that resets `_currentChangedIndex` to `-1`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/44a225758b78438ccca2a32e94e1871cc845cdd9/src/vs/workbench/contrib/notebook/browser/diff/notebookDiffEditor.ts#L574).
2. [`_list.clear()`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/44a225758b78438ccca2a32e94e1871cc845cdd9/src/vs/workbench/contrib/notebook/browser/diff/notebookDiffEditor.ts#L544) then clears the focus, but that listener is no longer present.

Previously, `clearInput()` spliced the list while the listener was still active. The new ordering leaves a cached pane's public `currentChangedIndex` at the previous input's value. The [chat notebook-diff integration reads this observable](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/44a225758b78438ccca2a32e94e1871cc845cdd9/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatEditing/notebook/chatEditingNotebookEditorIntegration.ts#L687), including for [navigation-boundary decisions](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/44a225758b78438ccca2a32e94e1871cc845cdd9/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatEditing/notebook/chatEditingNotebookEditorIntegration.ts#L715).

**Suggested repro / regression test (source-derived; not executed):**

1. Use the notebook text-diff editor with `notebook.experimental.enableNewDiffEditor: false` and `notebook.diff.enablePreview: true`.
2. Compare two notebooks with at least three changed cells. Focus the third change and verify the pane's `currentChangedIndex.get()` is `2`.
3. Close the diff without disposing its editor group/pane cache. In a debugger or focused pane test, inspect that same pane immediately after `clearInput()` returns, before a subsequent input/list update.
4. **Expected:** `currentChangedIndex.get()` is `-1`. **Source-predicted result at this head:** it remains `2`. Also cover replacing the input in the same pane so the old selection does not survive into the replacement's loading interval.

Please explicitly reset `_currentChangedIndex` to `-1` during detachment and retain focused clear/reuse coverage. The reset briefly added in `30550d45` was removed by the head revert; moving it to separate #339389 does not include it in this PR's standalone delta.

**Validation limit:** both independent source reviews identified the ordering regression, but no Code OSS reproduction or visible chat-navigation failure was demonstrated. The pane's own next/previous commands use list focus and are not claimed broken. This is a low-severity observable-state regression, not a claim of a broad navigation outage.
Should be resolved with PR https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339389, which is now merged.
